excerpt: What makes a crash witness credible, why independent witnesses matter most, and how their accounts get tested.
keyTakeaways: Credible car accident witnesses are independent, had clear vantage points, provide consistent and specific accounts, and give testimony corroborated by physical evidence. Georgia follows the Daubert standard for expert testimony (O.C.G.A. § 24-7-702) and allows two years to file (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33). South Carolina has not adopted Daubert but applies a similar reliability test under Rule 702, SCRE (State v. Council), and provides three years (S.C. Code § 15-3-530). Both states use modified comparative fault rules where witness testimony is critical to determining each party's percentage of responsibility.

faqs.question: What makes a witness credible in a car accident case?
faqs.answer: The most credible witnesses are independent (no relationship to either driver), had a clear vantage point, provide consistent accounts over time, offer specific details about what happened, remain calm and straightforward when testifying, and give testimony that is corroborated by physical evidence and other witnesses.

faqs.question: Can a passenger be a witness in a car accident case?
faqs.answer: Yes, passengers can testify as witnesses. However, because they have a relationship with the driver, their testimony may carry less weight than that of an independent bystander. Insurance adjusters and defense attorneys may argue that a passenger witness is biased, so corroborating evidence strengthens their testimony.

faqs.question: How do I find witnesses after a car accident?
faqs.answer: At the accident scene, look for other drivers who stopped, pedestrians, cyclists, and people in nearby businesses. Get their names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Note where they were positioned. Also check for dashcams, doorbell cameras, and business security cameras, and ask quickly before footage is recorded over; state DOT traffic cameras in Georgia and South Carolina do not record. Video must be authenticated and can be challenged in court. Contact an attorney promptly so they can follow up while memories are fresh.

faqs.question: What is an expert witness in a car accident case?
faqs.answer: Expert witnesses are professionals retained for their specialized knowledge. Common experts in car accident cases include accident reconstructionists who recreate the collision, medical experts who testify about injuries, biomechanical engineers who explain crash forces, vocational experts who assess work impact, and economists who calculate financial losses.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Georgia or South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Georgia gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33. South Carolina allows three years under S.C. Code § 15-3-530. Because witness memories fade over time, it is critical to contact an attorney and obtain witness statements as early as possible.

faqs.question: Can a witness with a criminal record testify in my car accident case?
faqs.answer: Yes, a person with a criminal record can still testify as a witness. However, in both Georgia and South Carolina, opposing counsel can generally use a witness's felony convictions, and any conviction for a crime involving dishonesty or a false statement, to challenge the witness's credibility, usually only if the conviction is less than ten years old (O.C.G.A. § 24-6-609; Rule 609, SCRE). Georgia does not count nolo contendere pleas or first-offender discharges. A criminal record does not automatically disqualify a witness, but it may reduce the weight given to their testimony.
